species.real: In the First World War dried sphagnum moss was gathered by the sackful for wound dressings, because it soaks up blood and is mildly antiseptic.
species.name: Sphagnet

dex.text: Soft, damp and very patient, it holds water like a grudge. Pleasantly cool in summer, and a little smug about it.
dex.fact: Sphagnum moss can hold many times its own weight in water, which is why bogs stay so soggy.

species.real: Peatlands cover only about three per cent of the world's land, but they hold roughly twice as much carbon as all its forests put together.
species.name: Peatmonarch

dex.text: Ruler of the moss, slow and bulky. Takes centuries to make a decision, but once made, the decision stays made.
dex.fact: Peat builds up very slowly, often less than a millimetre a year, so a deep bog is a very old bog.
